questions.question: What colour are the zig-zag lines at a zebra or pelican crossing?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 uses white zig-zag lines on both sides of crossings.

questions.question: What colour are the criss-cross lines of a box junction?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 marks box junctions with yellow criss-cross lines.

questions.question: How much room should you give a cyclist when overtaking at 25 mph?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 states at least 1.5 metres at speeds up to 30 mph.

questions.question: In dry weather, what is the two-second rule used for?
options: Keeping a safe stopping gap behind the vehicle ahead
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses the two-second rule to keep a safe gap.

questions.question: Who needs to see your signal before you turn?
options: Other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 says signals warn all road users of your plans.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a signed 20 mph zone?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires obeying signed speed limits including 20 mph zones.

questions.question: What is the red and amber phase useful for while you wait behind the line?
options: Getting ready to move off safely once green appears
questions.explain: Rule 175: use red and amber to prepare to move off and check around you, not to cross the line early.

questions.question: Before joining a busier road from a give-way line, where should you look?
options: Both right and left for vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells you to look both ways for all road users before pulling out.

questions.question: If a pedestrian has already stepped into the road you are turning into, what must you do?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 170 says you must give way to pedestrians already crossing the road you are turning into.

questions.question: When should you switch on your left indicator before turning left?
options: In good time before slowing and turning
Only if a car is behind
questions.explain: Rule 182 and Rule 103 say to give a clear left signal in good time.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how should your move affect vehicles in the next lane?
options: They should slow down slightly for you
You must not force them to slow down or swerve
You only need to clear cars behind you
You have priority if you signal first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 states you must not cut in or force others to slow down.

questions.question: When may you move onto the right-hand side of a two-way road?
options: When overtaking or passing a parked vehicle safely
questions.explain: Rule 160: you only move right when overtaking, passing an obstruction, or turning right, and when it is safe.

questions.question: When is it safe to enter a roundabout?
options: When there is a safe gap so circulating traffic does not have to slow down
Whenever you reach the line first
Whenever the car in front enters, without looking
Only after stopping for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises entering only when there is a safe gap to the right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when going straight ahead at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: When turning right at a roundabout, what should you do with your signal before leaving?
options: Keep signalling right until you are on the new road
Switch from right signal to left signal just after the exit before yours
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to signal left after passing the exit before your right-turn exit.

questions.question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 explains the blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

questions.question: Where must a car driver stop on red when there is an advanced stop line?
options: Behind the first white line before the cycle box
questions.explain: Rule 178: you must stop at the first white line so the cycle box stays clear for cyclists.

questions.question: In Great Britain, may you turn left at a red traffic light if the road is clear?
options: No, you must wait for green
Yes, if no pedestrians are waiting
questions.explain: Rule 175: unlike some countries, there is no turn on red in Great Britain unless a green arrow shows.

questions.question: What happens if you drift sideways out of your lane on a roundabout?
options: You could collide with a car or cyclist beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against cutting across another driver's lane when circulating.

questions.question: If the main road looks completely empty at a stop sign, may you roll slowly through?
options: No, your wheels must stop completely first
questions.explain: Rule 171: a stop sign is a legal must rule: you must come to a full standstill before moving out.

questions.question: Why should you choose your roundabout approach lane early?
options: To avoid last-second swerving across other drivers
So you do not need signals
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 encourages early lane selection for smooth, safe driving.

questions.question: You are 40 metres away at 30 mph when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Brake smoothly and stop behind the line
questions.explain: Rule 175: at 30 mph, 40 metres is plenty of room to stop safely behind the line.

questions.question: If there is a central refuge island on a zebra crossing, how is it treated?
questions.explain: Rule 195: a central island splits it into two separate crossings, though you should still watch carefully.

questions.question: At a roundabout with three approach lanes, the middle lane is marked straight ahead. Which lane should you use to go straight?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to follow painted lane markings on multi-lane approaches.

questions.question: You are two metres from the stop line at 30 mph with a car close behind when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Stop in the middle of the junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: you are too close to stop safely, so continuing through is the safer choice.

questions.question: Where does the no-overtaking rule at a zebra crossing apply?
options: Within the zig-zag zone on the approach to the crossing
Only on the black and white stripes
Only after you pass the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies across the zig-zag markings approaching the crossing.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but cars are queued just past the box junction. What should you do?
options: Drive into the box so cars behind you can cross
Wait behind the junction until space opens beyond the box
Sound your horn to make the queue move
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says you must wait before the box even on a green light if the exit is blocked.

questions.question: What should you do if a cyclist is riding in the middle of the lane in slow town traffic?
options: Stay patiently behind them and do not force past
Sound your horn until they move over
Squeeze past inches from their handlebar
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and H1/H2 respect cyclists' safe road position.

questions.question: What should you do if a car pulls into your safe two-second gap?
options: Sound your horn and stay close
Ease off gently to rebuild your two-second gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 advises dropping back smoothly whenever the gap shrinks.

questions.question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

questions.question: Can you drive above the speed limit briefly while overtaking?
options: Yes, for up to five seconds
No, you must never exceed the speed limit
Yes, if no cameras are nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 makes clear that speed limits are the legal maximum at all times.

questions.question: When the light changes from red and amber to green, what should you check before moving?
options: That the junction is clear of late crossers and pedestrians
questions.explain: Rule 175: green means you may go on if the way is clear; watch for late crossers.

questions.question: When turning left into a side road, where should you look for waiting pedestrians?
options: Along the pavement and crossing point of the side road
questions.explain: Rule H2: scan the side road pavement early before you start steering into the turn.

questions.question: If the lane you want to enter has faster traffic, what should you do?
options: Pull out and let them brake
Wait for a safe gap so they do not have to slow down
Signal for one second then steer
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires waiting so faster vehicles do not have to slow down.

questions.question: If you pass a row of parked cars on your left, what should you do afterwards?
options: Return to the left when there is room
questions.explain: Rule 160: move back to the left once past the parked cars so oncoming traffic has space.

questions.question: What should you also watch for before entering a roundabout besides cars?
options: Cyclists, motorcyclists, and pedestrians crossing the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds drivers to watch out for cyclists, riders, and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which signal do you give on approach when going straight ahead (second exit)?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: What should you check in your mirrors just before signalling left to leave an inner roundabout lane?
options: Check your left mirror and blind spot for cars or cyclists beside you
Only look at the central island
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to watch for traffic on your left before moving out to exit.

questions.question: At a painted mini-roundabout, how should you pass the white circle when turning right?
options: Drive clockwise around the painted circle if possible
Cut straight across the wrong side of the circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 188 and Rule 185 state all vehicles must pass around the central marking clockwise.

questions.question: Why should you not stop inside the cycle box even if no cyclist is there yet?
options: Cyclists may ride up the left side to use it
questions.explain: Rule 178: cyclists filter forward to reach the box safely before the lights change.

questions.question: You see a car approaching from the right with its left indicator on. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are sure it is actually turning before pulling out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 warns never to assume a flashing indicator means the driver will turn.

questions.question: When two exit lanes merge after a roundabout, how should you leave?
options: Stay in your exit lane cleanly, then merge smoothly when safe
Squeeze both cars side by side into one lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps exits orderly until lanes merge safely downstream.

questions.question: If a main road has two lanes in one direction and you turn left onto it, which lane should you join?
options: The left-hand lane unless road signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 and lane rules keep turning traffic in the left lane when clear.

questions.question: At 60 mph, roughly how far does a car travel in two seconds?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 shows two seconds scales automatically with higher speed.

questions.question: What should you check before cancelling a signal early if you change your mind?
options: That nobody has already reacted to your first signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses clear, unambiguous signals at all times.

questions.question: If a car is towing a trailer on a dual carriageway, does it share the 70 mph car limit?
options: No, towing vehicles have a lower 60 mph limit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets a 60 mph limit for cars towing trailers on dual carriageways.

questions.question: In heavy rain, why do blind-spot checks matter even more before changing lanes?
options: Spray reduces what you can see in side mirrors
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and wet-weather advice warn that spray hides vehicles in mirrors.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.

questions.question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.

questions.question: On a dual-lane exit roundabout where both lanes lead straight ahead, how should you pick your approach lane?
options: Use the left lane unless you are overtaking or signs direct otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps traffic left unless overtaking or directed by markings.
